methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: According to the international standard ISO 50006–2014 [14], an EPI (Energy Performance Indicator) is a value or measure that quantiﬁes energy efﬁciency, energy use and energy use performance in facilities, systems, processes and equipment. Organizations use EPIs as a measure of their energy performance. To decide on which indicator is relevant, a statistical analysis is necessary to highlight the best correlated indicator in each context.

evidence_quote: International standard : ISO 50001:2018 Energy management systems — Requirements with guidance for use
International standard ISO 50006:2014 Energy management systems — Measuring energy performance using energy baselines (EnB) and energy performance indicators (EnPI) — General principles and guidance

Collect energy data of all government hospital buildings and a regression analysis was performed based on the feedback to predict the annual energy consumption. Multiple indicators from data, which are assumed to be ones that have major inﬂuences, were selected for the study of their sensitivity to annual energy consumption.
The most widely used relevant indicator in the health sector is the annual energy consumption per bed (kWh/bed/year).
